candidate_relations.reason: The clinical picture of sudden-onset limb weakness in a previously healthy young woman with EMG changes extending well beyond the AIN territory (biceps brachii, triceps brachii, deltoid) is characteristic of Parsonage-Turner Syndrome presenting with predominant AIN involvement. Labeling this solely as AIN Syndrome misses the broader brachial plexus/neuralgic amyotrophy etiology and the multi-muscle EMG findings that are incompatible with a pure AIN lesion.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Anterior Interosseous Nerve Syndrome describes the anatomical distribution of weakness but does not capture the broader neuralgic amyotrophy (Parsonage-Turner Syndrome) etiology, which is evidenced by the EMG showing involvement beyond the AIN territory (biceps, triceps, deltoid) and the episodic, sudden onset in a young healthy woman

case_quality_flags: EMG findings extending to biceps, triceps, and deltoid are a key discriminator favoring Parsonage-Turner Syndrome over isolated AIN syndrome
